The content is exactly the interface, so it is short by design — but it is not nothing:
writing it is what turns "DAT-G produces a datum over `k'`, and separately DAT-J wants one
over `k`" into a single arrow, and it is what makes the remaining DAT-J debt *visibly* two
statements (the DAT-G descent, and the quasi-compactness) rather than an unspecified
assembly.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicRepDatum.toJacobianData` — DJ-IN: a `PicRepDatum k k C` plus
  quasi-compactness of its representing object is a `JacobianData C`, with `J`, `rep` and
  `lft` carried across unchanged.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicRepDatum.toJacobianData_J` / `_rep` — the two projections, `rfl`, so
  a consumer never unfolds the packaging.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicRepDatum.toJacobianDataOfAbelLifts` — the same with quasi-compactness
  supplied in the shape the classical argument delivers it: per-point residue-field lifts of
  an Abel morphism out of `DivScheme g` (`Picard/JacobianDataAbelSurj.lean`).

## What this does NOT do

It produces no `PicRepDatum`.  That is DAT-G/DAT-G0 — the finite-Galois descent from a
finite separable stage, whose one avatar-less core is `Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit`
(`Picard/PicRepColimitCompat.lean`), and it is divRep-gated.  Nor does it produce the
quasi-compactness or an Abel lift.  What it removes is the *assembly* step between them.
-/

35	Four things, and none of them says where a piece lives:
36	
37	* a per-piece **reading** `read j : H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ)) → Γ(pieces j)` — a local trivialization of the
38	  twist over the piece, which is what `relThetaResSide` *is* when the piece happens to lie in
39	  a chart;
40	* a per-pair **comparison unit** `unit i j` on the overlap;
41	* the **matching law** relating the two through that unit — the only input of
42	  `thetaEval_mem`;
43	* a **germ law** tying the reading to the two chart components up to a unit of the stalk,
44	  which is what the kernel bridge runs on.
45	
46	`ThetaTrivData` below packages exactly those.  It mentions `relPinnedChart` — the twist's own
47	model — and it says **nothing** about `pieces j ≤ anything`.
48	
49	## What this buys, proved rather than asserted
50	
51	* `ChartTyping.thetaTrivData` — the old index maps in, so nothing landed is lost and the
52	  chart-typed layer is the special case it always was.
53	* `thetaTrivData_zero` — **`ThetaTrivData D 0` is inhabited for EVERY widened cover**,
54	  straddling ones included, by gluing the two chart components over the piece (the sheaf
55	  axiom for `V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤`, applied to the piece — not a confinement of the piece, which is
56	  covered by the two charts rather than contained in one).
57	* `nonempty_thetaTrivData_and_isEmpty_chartTyping` — **the separation**: on a straddling
58	  cover the new index is inhabited while `ChartTyping` is empty.  So this is a strictly wider
59	  index, on exactly the covers `I-0492` is about, and the exponent it is proved at is the one
60	  `DivisorAdaptation.divisorDatum` runs at (`thetaIdealUnit_zero`,
61	  `Picard/DivisorDatumInverse.lean:207`) — not a vacuous corner.
62	
63	## What it does NOT buy, stated plainly
64	
65	Inhabitation at `a > 0` needs `𝒪(Θᵃ)` to be trivial over each piece, which for an arbitrary
66	affine open is a condition on the bundle (a class in `Pic` of the piece), **not** free.  This
67	file makes that a hypothesis about the SHEAF that a producer may discharge per cover, in place
68	of an index that no straddling cover can inhabit at all.  The `a > 0` producer is not here and
69	is not claimed.
70	-/

101	  over `pieces j`, spelled through its effect on sections. -/
102	  read : ∀ j : D.index, relThetaSections C R π a →ₗ[R] Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)

104	  unit : ∀ i j : D.index, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j)ˣ
105	  /-- **The matching law**: on the overlap the two readings differ by the comparison unit.
106	  This is the whole input of `thetaEval_mem`. -/

108	    (relCurve C R).resHom (inf_le_left : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces i) (read i x)

111	        * (relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_right (read j x)

113	  the reading agrees with the germ of that chart's component of the section up to a unit of
114	  the stalk.  This is what the kernel bridge runs on, and it refers to the two-chart model of
115	  the SHEAF rather than to the location of the piece.

117	  Stated in the `relThetaResSide … inf_le_right` spelling rather than as `Bool.rec x.val.1

123	      ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) z hzj).hom (read j x)
124	        = (u : (relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk z)
125	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ ((⊤ : (relCurve C R).Opens) ⊓ relPinnedChart C R π b)

135	assigned side, the unit is `AffAdaptation.thetaOvlUnit`, the matching law is
136	`relThetaResSide_matching` — i.e. exactly the three ingredients
137	`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffTheta.lean` uses — and the germ law holds with `u = 1` on the assigned
138	side, comparing the two sides through the side matching unit otherwise.

141	index, it does not replace one theory by another. -/
142	noncomputable def thetaTrivData : ThetaTrivData (π := π) D a where
143	  read j := relThetaResSide a (τ.side j)
144	    (AffAdaptation.piece_le_relPinnedChart (π := π) τ j)
145	  unit i j := relThetaSideUnit a (τ.side i) (τ.side j)
146	    (AffAdaptation.pieces_inf_le_relPinnedChart_inf (π := π) τ i j)
147	  matching i j x := by
148	    rw [resHom_relThetaResSide a (τ.side i)
149	        (AffAdaptation.piece_le_relPinnedChart (π := π) τ i),
150	      resHom_relThetaResSide a (τ.side j)
151	        (AffAdaptation.piece_le_relPinnedChart (π := π) τ j)]
152	    exact relThetaResSide_matching a (τ.side i) (τ.side j)
153	      (AffAdaptation.pieces_inf_le_relPinnedChart_inf (π := π) τ i j) x
154	  germ_read j b z hzj hzb x := by
155	    -- the two readings at `z` differ by the side matching unit, restricted to a germ
156	    have hzW : z ∈ D.pieces j ⊓ relPinnedChart C R π b := ⟨hzj, hzb⟩
157	    have hle : D.pieces j ⊓ relPinnedChart C R π b
158	        ≤ relPinnedChart C R π (τ.side j) ⊓ relPinnedChart C R π b :=
159	      inf_le_inf_right _ (AffAdaptation.piece_le_relPinnedChart (π := π) τ j)
160	    have hmatch := relThetaResSide_matching a (τ.side j) b hle x
161	    -- the comparison unit already lives on the piece-chart overlap, so its germ is a unit
162	    refine ⟨(((relThetaSideUnit a (τ.side j) b hle).isUnit).map
163	      ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j ⊓ relPinnedChart C R π b) z hzW).hom).unit, ?_⟩
164	    have hgerm := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
165	      (D.pieces j ⊓ relPinnedChart C R π b) z hzW).hom hmatch
166	    rw [map_mul] at hgerm
167	    -- move the reading's germ down to the overlap, where `hmatch` lives
168	    rw [show ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) z hzj).hom
169	          (relThetaResSide a (τ.side j)
170	            (AffAdaptation.piece_le_relPinnedChart (π := π) τ j) x)
171	        = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j ⊓ relPinnedChart C R π b) z hzW).hom
172	            (relThetaResSide a (τ.side j) (hle.trans inf_le_left) x) from
173	      (AffAdaptation.germ_relThetaResSide_eq a x (τ.side j)
174	        (AffAdaptation.piece_le_relPinnedChart (π := π) τ j) inf_le_left hzW).symm,
175	      hgerm]
176	    -- and the `b`-component's germ up from the overlap to `⊤ ⊓ chart b`

178	      (inf_le_right : (⊤ : (relCurve C R).Opens) ⊓ relPinnedChart C R π b
179	        ≤ relPinnedChart C R π b)

186	At `a = 0` the theta cocycle is trivial (`relThetaCocycle_zero`), so a global theta section is

235	    show relThetaResSide 0 j (hle.trans inf_le_right) x
236	      = (relCurve C R).resHom (inf_le_right :

354	
355	Everything here is the corresponding declaration of `Picard/DivisorFamilyAffTheta.lean` with
356	`τ : ChartTyping` replaced by `T : ThetaTrivData`, and it is a genuine re-indexing rather than
357	a copy: each proof below invokes exactly one field of `T` where the chart-typed version invoked
358	`relThetaResSide`/`relThetaResSide_matching` at `τ.side j`.  That correspondence is what
359	`ChartTyping.thetaTrivData` makes precise — the old layer is the special case.
360	
361	The point of doing it here rather than editing that file: its declarations stay valid and
362	consumed, and a producer may now choose either index.  `AffCoverData.thetaTrivDataZero` gives
363	the widened one on every cover. -/

365	namespace AffAdaptation

367	variable {D : AffCoverData C R} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
368	variable (A : AffAdaptation D d) {a : ℕ} (T : ThetaTrivData (π := π) D a)

370	/-- **The Θ-twisted right overlap arrow**, twisted by the datum's comparison unit. -/
371	noncomputable def trivDeltaRight : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
372	  LinearMap.pi (fun p : D.index × D.index =>
373	    LinearMap.mulLeft R (Ideal.Quotient.mk (A.ovlIdeal p.1 p.2)
374	        ((T.unit p.1 p.2 : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2)ˣ) :
375	          Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces p.1 ⊓ D.pieces p.2))) ∘ₗ
376	      (A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.2)
377	
378	/-- **The Θ-twisted glued colength module `W(d)^{Θᵃ}` over a chart-free datum.** -/
379	noncomputable def trivGluedSubmodule : Submodule R A.chartProd :=
380	  LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - trivDeltaRight A T)
381	
382	lemma mem_trivGluedSubmodule_iff (s : A.chartProd) :
383	    s ∈ trivGluedSubmodule A T ↔ ∀ p : D.index × D.index,
384	      A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2 (s p.1)

412	`relThetaResSide_matching`, this calls the datum's `matching` field — the only input. -/
413	theorem trivEval_mem (x : relThetaSections C R π a) :
414	    trivEval A T x ∈ trivGluedSubmodule A T := by
415	  rw [mem_trivGluedSubmodule_iff]
416	  rintro ⟨i, j⟩
417	  rw [trivEval_apply, trivEval_apply, toOvlLeft_mk, toOvlRight_mk, ← map_mul]
418	  exact congrArg _ (T.matching i j x)
419	
420	/-- **The evaluation `H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ)) → W(d)^{Θᵃ}` over a chart-free datum.** -/
421	noncomputable def trivGluedEval :
422	    relThetaSections C R π a →ₗ[R] TrivGlued A T :=
423	  LinearMap.codRestrict (trivGluedSubmodule A T) (trivEval A T) (trivEval_mem A T)
424

426	    LinearMap.ker (trivGluedEval A T) = LinearMap.ker (trivEval A T) :=

432	(`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffTheta.lean:813`): there the germ of the reading IS the germ of the
433	assigned chart component (the reading is a restriction), here it agrees with it up to a unit of
434	the stalk — and a stalk ideal is closed under multiplication by units, so the argument is
435	unchanged.  That unit is precisely the slack that buys chart-freedom. -/
436	
437	/-- **The germ of the reading of a killed section lies in `d`'s stalk ideal**, at a point of the
438	piece, read against any pinned chart containing it.  The chart-free counterpart of
439	`germ_val_mem_stalkIdeal_of_thetaEval_eq_zero`. -/
440	lemma germ_read_mem_stalkIdeal_of_trivEval_eq_zero {x : relThetaSections C R π a}
441	    (hker : ∀ j, trivEval A T x j = 0) (b : Bool) (j : D.index)
442	    {z : relCurve C R} (hzj : z ∈ D.pieces j) (hzb : z ∈ relPinnedChart C R π b) :
443	    ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ ((⊤ : (relCurve C R).Opens) ⊓ relPinnedChart C R π b)
444	        z ⟨trivial, hzb⟩).hom (relThetaResSide a b inf_le_right x) ∈ d.stalkIdeal z := by

446	  -- the reading's germ is in the stalk ideal: the evaluation vanishes on the piece
447	  have hgermread : ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) z hzj).hom (T.read j x)
448	      ∈ d.stalkIdeal z := by
449	    have hmem : T.read j x ∈ Ideal.span {A.eqn j} := by
450	      have h := hker j
451	      rw [trivEval_apply, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem] at h
452	      exact h
453	    obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := Ideal.mem_span_singleton.mp hmem
454	    have hgerm := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) z hzj).hom hc

479	  ext x

481	  constructor

489	      simpa using h

494	    rw [germ_eqn_span_eq_stalkIdeal A j hz]

502	      · exact ⟨true, hb⟩

504	    obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := T.germ_read j b z hz hzb x
505	    rw [hu]

507	      (germ_val_mem_stalkIdeal_of_forall_side a x h b ⟨trivial, hzb⟩)

`Picard/JacobianDataFromPicRepDatum.lean` reduced DAT-J to two inputs: a
`PicRepDatum k k C` and, for every point `y` of the representing object, a lift

> `∃ q : Spec κ(y) ⟶ DivScheme g, q ≫ abel = fromSpecResidueField y`.

The lift has been read as "the Abel map is surjective on points", i.e. as geometry still
to be done. **The morphism half is already built**, in a rooted file, and what is missing
is only that it sits over the right point.

## What is landed, and had no consumer

`Picard/DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean` (rooted, sorry-free) carries the whole *fibrewise*
chain, and the reason it is short is that **over a field the certificate is free**:

* `DivisorAdaptation.isCertified_of_deg` (`:104`) — over a field `K`, an adaptation whose
  presentation divisor has degree `n` is `IsCertified n`.  All seven clauses: projectivity
  and both flat-cokernel clauses are `Module.Free.of_divisionRing` instances, `(c1)`
  finiteness is `moduleFinite_colength`, and the `(c2)` rank clause is the *unconditional*
  CRT identity `deg_presentationDivisor` read against the degree hypothesis.  No support
  separation is needed — which the file records as a deviation of record, since full
  support separation is unachievable when a support point lies in both charts' overlap.
* `exists_divFam_divFamDivisor_eq` (`:147`) — hence every effective degree-`g` divisor over
  `K` *is* the divisor of a `DivFam`.
* `effectiveDivisorClassifyZar` (`:217`) — and it classifies, giving
  `overSpec k K ⟶ divSchemeOver …`, characterized by `effectiveDivisorClassifyZar_spec`
  (`:231`).

This is the sharp form of critical-path §7.6's own observation that the `DivFamZar` no-go
is a purely *relative* phenomenon, **vacuous over a field**: the difficulty that makes U2
hard does not exist fibrewise.

## What is therefore actually missing

`effectiveDivisorClassifyZar_spec` says the morphism is `divRepClassifyZar` of a family
